original.description: A French Hotchkiss mle 1914 machine gun photographed against a plain ground. The Commons record's description names both the object and the holding institution in one line: "French machine-gun Hotchkiss model 1914 (in coll. Mémorial de Verdun)". The file sits in the Commons categories "Hotchkiss Mle 14", "Verdun Memorial" and "Machine guns on white background".
original.photographer: Jean-Frédéric (Wikimedia Commons contributor, signing as historicair), 13 October 2006
original.date: 13 October 2006 (the photograph); the object is a Hotchkiss mle 1914, the French heavy machine gun of the war — the 1914 pattern was the successor to the mle 1900 that the French army had in the field in August
original.archive: Mémorial de Verdun, Fleury-devant-Douaumont (the collection); photograph held on Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: CC BY-SA 3.0 (Commons record: LicenseShortName "CC BY-SA 3.0"; UsageTerms "Creative Commons Attribution-Share Alike 3.0"; AttributionRequired true; the record also offers GFDL and CC BY-SA 2.5/2.0/1.0). Attribution to the photographer is mandatory and the share-alike condition applies to derivatives.

colorization.status: not colorized, and must not be — a modern colour photograph of the object, and the licence is share-alike.

content_policy: ok — a museum object photographed on its own; no casualties
caption: The Hotchkiss mle 1914, the French heavy machine gun — gas-operated and air-cooled where the German and British guns were water-cooled Maxims. Collection of the Mémorial de Verdun.
notes: Verified 2026-08-25 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API (Artist, Credit, DateTimeOriginal, LicenseShortName, UsageTerms, AttributionRequired, Permission read from extmetadata). Two better-known alternatives were passed over on identification rather than licence: the Musée de l'Armée files by Rama carry no object name in their description at all — only the file title asserts what is in the frame — and a card must not be captioned from a file name. A Springfield Armory Museum catalogue photograph (File:Hotchkiss model 1914 MG.jpg, public domain, serial 26634) has the better record but is only 629 × 480. A caution for the card when it is written: the mle 1914 is the pattern the French army fought most of the war with, and in August 1914 the machine-gun companies still had the mle 1900 alongside it. No `used_by`: the machine-gun card does not exist yet, for the reason recorded on the MG 08 manifest and in docs/imagery-kit.md.
credit: Photograph: Jean-Frédéric (historicair), 2006, of an object in the collection of the Mémorial de Verdun; via Wikimedia Commons; CC BY-SA 3.0.
